summary.text: Young Kim is a Republican who was born in Incheon, South Korea, worked as a financial analyst and as a longtime aide to Rep. Ed Royce, and served in the California State Assembly from 2014 to 2016. She has been in the U.S. House since January 2021 and serves on the Financial Services and Foreign Affairs committees, where she chairs the East Asia and the Pacific Subcommittee. Redistricting placed her in the same new 40th District as fellow Republican incumbent Ken Calvert, and she is running on her record in Congress.

paragraphs.text: Born in Incheon, South Korea, in 1962 and raised in Seoul; her family left South Korea in 1975, living first in Guam and then Hawaii, according to Wikipedia. Her official biography describes her as an immigrant.
Earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from the University of Southern California in 1985.

Worked as a financial analyst at First Interstate Bank and as a controller at JK Sportswear Manufacturing, and started her own clothing-industry business, according to Wikipedia; her official biography calls her a small business owner.

Worked for Ed Royce, first in his state Senate office and then for 21 years in his congressional office as community liaison and director of Asian affairs, according to Wikipedia; Ballotpedia lists her as his director of community relations and Asian affairs.
Represented District 65 in the California State Assembly from 2014 to 2016, winning in 2014 over Democratic incumbent Sharon Quirk-Silva and losing to Quirk-Silva in 2016.

Ran for the open California 39th Congressional District in 2018 and lost to Democrat Gil Cisneros, 51.6% to 48.4%; won the 2020 rematch and was sworn in on January 3, 2021, as one of the first Korean American women in Congress.

Ran for re-election in the 40th District after the 2021 redistricting and won again in 2024; in the 119th Congress she serves on the Financial Services and Foreign Affairs committees, chairs the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on East Asia and the Pacific, and serves on the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party.
According to her official biography, she and her husband Charles live in Anaheim Hills and have four children and two grandchildren; Ballotpedia lists her residence as La Habra.
